_comment: Winter '27 (release 264 / API 68.0) probe EXTENSION for scale-out wave R3-05 (batches C-I, 64 skills). One probe per defect class the writer+adversarial-reviewer recipe corrected in those skills. Unlike winter27-probes.json, not every fact here is new in Winter '27: several are long-standing facts the skills had wrong (marked era: longstanding). Arm A (no skill) may already be right on those; the lift of interest is on era: winter27 rows and on arm B never repeating the package's old wrong answer. Quotes are verbatim lines from scratchpad/corpus264/*.txt (grep -n on the 264 text). Built 2026-10-20.

probes.question: How many platform event messages can a single platform event-triggered flow interview receive in one batch?
probes.wrong_answer: Up to 2,000 event messages per batch, the same as an Apex trigger.
probes.correct_answer: Up to 200 event messages per batch for a flow (2,000 is the Apex trigger batch size).
probes.quote: A flow can receive a batch of event messages at once, up to a maximum of 200 event messages.
probes.wrong_source: skills/flow/flow-platform-events-integration before batch F: 'up to 2,000 per batch'

probes.question: When a platform event-triggered flow creates or updates records, which user's context does the flow interview run in?
probes.wrong_answer: The Automated Process user, because the flow is subscribed to the event and runs asynchronously.
probes.correct_answer: The user who published the event message; only the debug logs appear under the Automated Process user.
probes.quote: each flow interview runs in the context of the user who published the event message.
probes.wrong_source: skills/flow/flow-platform-events-integration before batch F: 'runs as Automated Process user'

probes.question: How is a DataWeave script that Apex invokes stored and deployed in a Salesforce org?
probes.wrong_answer: As a static resource (.resource file) that Apex loads at run time.
probes.correct_answer: As DataWeaveResource metadata (a .dwl file with its -meta.xml under dw/), invoked directly from Apex.
probes.quote: You can create DataWeave scripts as metadata and invoke them directly from Apex.
probes.wrong_source: skills/integration/dataweave-for-apex before batch F: scripts stored as static resources

probes.question: In the Winter '27 (API 68.0) Metadata API, what is the product name used for the AI-powered change and release management experience that replaced the 'next-generation DevOps Center' wording?
probes.quote: Indicates whether the Lifecycle Center is enabled: true or false.

probes.question: Besides DefaultMode, SystemModeWithSharing and SystemModeWithoutSharing, is there a fourth Flow runInMode value in API 68.0, and what does it do?
probes.wrong_answer: No. The only values are DefaultMode, SystemModeWithSharing and SystemModeWithoutSharing; user context is only reachable through DefaultMode.
probes.correct_answer: Yes: UserMode (API 68.0 and later) runs the flow with the user's security context explicitly enforced, without inheriting sharing from the calling context.
probes.quote: UserMode—The flow runs with the user's security context explicitly enforced, without inheriting sharing settings from the calling context.
probes._note: Owner re-pointed 2026-10-20 after run 1: record-triggered-flow-patterns carries UserMode only in references/metadata-examples.md, which run_lift does not feed (arm B = SKILL.md + llm-anti-patterns.md); flow-governance SKILL.md holds the runInMode allow-list including UserMode. Run-1 result for this probe: A neither, B neither.

probes.question: What is the maximum size of a single Apex debug log, and what happens to a log that exceeds it?
probes.wrong_answer: 5 MB; anything past the limit is cut off at the end, so a missing EXECUTION_FINISHED line means truncation.
probes.correct_answer: 20 MB; larger logs are reduced by removing older log lines, which can be removed from any location, not just the start.
probes.quote: Each debug log must be 20 MB or smaller. Debug logs that are larger than 20 MB are reduced in size by removing older log lines
probes.wrong_source: skills/apex/salesforce-debug-log-analysis before batch H: '5MB per-log cap'

probes.question: How many batch Apex jobs can be held in the Apex flex queue, and what happens when Database.executeBatch is called while it is full?
probes.wrong_answer: 5 jobs in Holding or Queued; a sixth call is queued behind them.
probes.correct_answer: 100 jobs in Holding status; when the flex queue is full, Database.executeBatch throws a LimitException (the separate limit of 5 applies to queued-or-active jobs).
probes.quote: With the Apex flex queue, you can submit up to 100 batch jobs.
probes.wrong_source: skills/apex/scheduled-apex-failure-detection-and-monitoring before batch H: '5 batch jobs in Holding/Queued'

probes.question: When an unhandled exception occurs in asynchronous Apex such as a scheduled or batch job, who receives the unhandled exception email by default?
probes.wrong_answer: No one; exception emails are sent only for synchronous Apex, so async failures go only to the debug log.
probes.correct_answer: The developer in the LastModifiedBy field of the failing class or trigger, plus any Apex Exception Email recipients configured in Setup; this applies to asynchronous code too.
probes.quote: Unhandled exception emails are sent by default to the developer specified in the LastModifiedBy field on the failing class or trigger.
probes.wrong_source: skills/apex/scheduled-apex-failure-detection-and-monitoring before batch H: async exceptions 'email no one'

probes.question: How do you make Connect in Apex (ConnectApi) methods work inside an Apex test method?
probes.wrong_answer: Register a mock with Test.setMock(ConnectApi.ConnectApi.class, mockInstance) so no org data is needed.
probes.correct_answer: Most ConnectApi methods need real org data and fail unless the test is marked @IsTest(SeeAllData=true); some methods instead require a setTest* registration method named in the method's Usage section.
probes.quote: Most Connect in Apex methods require access to real org data, and fail unless used in test methods marked @IsTest(SeeAllData=true).

probes.question: What is the governor limit on callout time in a single Apex transaction, and is the 10-second figure a governor limit?
probes.wrong_answer: 10 seconds is the synchronous callout governor limit; exceeding it throws a LimitException that you can catch.
probes.correct_answer: The governor limit is 120 seconds cumulative across all callouts in the transaction; 10 seconds is only the default per-callout timeout (settable per request), and a LimitException cannot be caught.
probes.quote: Maximum cumulative timeout for all callouts (HTTP requests or Web services calls) in a           120 seconds           120 seconds
probes.wrong_source: skills/integration/middleware-integration-patterns before batch I: '10-second synchronous timeout' as a governor limit
